description: Deterministic dataset parameters shared byte-for-byte between the Java and Rust suites. The hot-path checksum is a pure function of each event's id, identical under every instrumentation variant — instrumentation must never change the business result. Each variant's side-effect counts (formatCount/loggedCount/droppedCount/distinctLabelsSeen/sampledCount) are also deterministic: the async-bounded-logging variant models a bounded queue's accept/drop decision synchronously at call time (no real background drain thread races the count), the same 'bounded reject' shape as the Backpressure and Bounded Pipelines lab applied to a log queue.

errorBurst.note: asyncQueueCapacity (16) is far below count (2000): the async-bounded-logging variant must drop 1984 of 2000 events by design, not fail.

highCardinalityKey.note: 500 distinct label keys over 2000 events exercises the metrics-labels variant's per-key bookkeeping cost.

stackTracePath.note: 12 stack frames of recursion before the hot path, so sampled-tracing's real stack-walk cost is representative.

correctnessInvariant: The hot-path checksum (XOR-accumulated across all events) is identical across every variant for a given dataset, in both languages. Side-effect counts satisfy: formatCount/loggedCount/droppedCount/distinctLabelsSeen/sampledCount match the deterministic rule for that variant exactly (e.g. ASYNC_BOUNDED_LOGGING: loggedCount == min(count, asyncQueueCapacity), droppedCount == count - loggedCount).
